title: What Resurrection Means for You Today — Ephesians 2:6
paragraphs: What Resurrection Means for You Today — Ephesians 2:6
He didn’t just rise for you—He raised you with Him.
That’s the part we rush past.
Ephesians 2:6 says God “raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus.”

Not will raise.
Not might raise.
Raised.
Already.
But look at your life.

Still fighting sin.
Still battling fear.
Still waking up with the same struggles.
So what does this even mean?
Here’s the tension:

You’re seated in victory…
while still walking through war.
And that’s where many believers break.

Because we feel low, we think we are low.
Because we struggle, we think we’re still slaves.

But resurrection didn’t just change Jesus’ location.
It changed your identity.

You are no longer fighting for approval.
You are fighting from a seated position of grace.
But here’s what we miss…

We keep crawling back to graves
that Jesus already emptied.

Old habits.
Old shame.
Old names people called you.
You visit them like they still have power.
They don’t.

The same power that pulled Christ out of the tomb
pulled you out of your old life.

Not partially.
Not temporarily.
Completely.
So why live like you're still buried?
This is resurrection for you today:

You don’t wake up trying to be worthy.
You wake up already seated with Christ.

You don’t earn victory.
You enforce it.

You don’t beg for identity.
You live from it.
And yes—some days you’ll feel weak.

But your position isn’t based on your feelings.
It’s anchored in Christ.
So stand up from what you’ve been lying in.

That sin? It’s not your home anymore.
That shame? It’s not your name anymore.
Jesus didn’t just rise…
He took you with Him.
